chunks: From him, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Humility is that you give people what you love to be given to you.

key_terms.التَّوَاضُعُ: Humility, modesty, or lowliness in status
key_terms.تُعْطَاهُ: To be given to you (passive form)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of humility in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) defines humility (al-tawadu') as the ethical practice of giving to others what one desires for oneself, emphasizing reciprocity and selflessness in social interactions. This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing humility not merely as lowliness, but as an active generosity that elevates the soul by prioritizing the needs of others. The concept reflects the Prophetic principle of 'giving what you love to give,' which is central to spiritual purification in Twelver Shi'ism.

en.hubeali:
From him, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The humbleness is that you give the people what you love that it be given to you’.
